new_statements.rule_in_words: Underlying vowels (with syncopated vowels restored) are footed left-to-right into iambs, a syllable with a long (strong) vowel being heavy and able to head a foot alone; every foot head carries (secondary) stress; feet are grouped right-to-left into left-headed cola and primary stress goes to the head of the rightmost colon, i.e. the head of the penultimate foot when there are two or more feet (surface 'nenˌwek 'men', ˌnesh'naˌbé 'Indian', ˌneshˌna'bémˌwen 'Indian language'); vowels in unstressed (weak) positions are reduced or deleted (syncope).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stress on the head of every iambic foot not bearing primary stress (e.g. ˌnesh'naˌbé, ˌneshˌna'bémˌwen, 'nenˌwek).
new_statements.exceptions: Degenerate feet rare or impossible; a few sub-minimal particles (se, zhe, je) and the verb be (padded with pleonastic -wak); word-initial short /o/ regularly survives in weak position (wgema 'chief'); syncope does not treat all weak vowels in weak positions alike in modern Potawatomi (some delete fully, some surface intact, partly Ojibwe influence); preverbs/prenouns are separate domains for syncope and stress (p. 27; ch. 3 fn.); word-final vowels are lengthened/strengthened (p. 40, citing Gathercole 1978:23). Author flags the analysis as a sketch expanded from Hayes (1995:221) and Lockwood (2012).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level metrical analysis of modern Forest County (Wisconsin) Potawatomi, stated over underlying forms; surface citation forms show primary stress on the penult in the worked examples. CONTRAST: Gathercole 1978 (instrumental, Kansas Potawatomi, saved held by the project) states accent is non-phonemic and phrase-level, high pitch 'regularly the third syllable from the end of the phrase, or the first vowel in a phrase of fewer than four syllables' (pp. 26-27) -- an antepenultimate phrase accent, not obviously reconcilable with Lockwood's colon rule.
new_statements.identity_note: Lockwood 2017 describes modern Potawatomi as spoken by the last L1 elders of the Forest County Potawatomi Community, northern Wisconsin ('Northern' Potawatomi); Gathercole 1978 measured Kansas (Prairie Band) Potawatomi speakers recorded in the 1970s ('Southern' Potawatomi). Glottolog pota1247 has no dialect-level codes; both fall under pota1247 / ISO pot.

sources.locator: Chapter 2 'Potawatomi Sounds', sec. 3.1 'Syllabification and Syncope', pp. 25-26 and 28-30 (foot inventory ex. 29; stress exx. 36-39; summary p. 30)
sources.note: Ch. 2 sec. 3.1 (pp. 24-30): syllables parsed L-to-R into iambic feet (long/strong vowels heavy); foot heads get secondary stress; feet grouped R-to-L into trochaic cola, primary stress on head of the rightmost colon; unstressed weak vowels syncopate. Examples 'nenˌwek 'men', ˌnesh'naˌbé 'Indian', ˌneshˌna'bémˌwen 'Indian language'. Also p. 40: word-final vowels lengthened/strengthened (citing Gathercole 1978:23).
